LESSON: GROUPING OF FOOD

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Foods
Topic 3.4: Grouping of food

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Grouping of food. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. mention foods from plant sources within their locality,
2. group foods according to the different parts of the plants that they come from,
3. mention different foods from animal sources within the locality,
4. appreciate the importance of animal and plants as sources of food. pictures or a video. grouping of food using computing devices food from plant and animal sources Competencies to be developed: Critical thinking and problem solving Links to PCIs: ESD – environmental education and animal welfare links to other subjects:

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Grouping of food.
2. Explain Grouping of food to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grouping of food.
4. Show that you can: mention foods from plant sources within their locality,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grouping of food. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Grouping of food important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER
